FarguesFontaineDiamonds.summary: Nothing in either library knows about diamonds, v-sheaves, Spd, perfectoid spaces or the Fargues–Fontaine curve: a case-insensitive sweep of both Lean trees finds no `Fargues`, no `Spd`, no `v-sheaf`/`vSheaf`, no `A_inf`, and the only `diamond` declarations are the modular-forms diamond operators. What does exist is the raw input the roadmap says it will consume: Mathlib's Witt vectors with Frobenius and Teichmüller, its tilting/perfection package (`PreTilt` with its valuation, `PreTilt.untilt`, and `Tilt` for a valued field), Fontaine's `θ` with surjectivity, and `BDeRhamPlus`/`BDeRham` for a general perfectoid ring; and Tau Ceti's Huber-ring and adic-spectrum theory (`IsHuberRing`, `PairOfDefinition`, `spa`, rational subsets, the analytic locus, localisation topologies, sheaf criteria). Genuinely missing is everything the roadmap actually asks for: A_inf with its `(p,[ϖ])`-adic Huber structure, the open `ᵀY_F = D(p)∩D([ϖ])`, the Frobenius quotient X_F, any category of adic spaces or morphisms between them, diamondification, and the étale-site comparisons. F0–F5 are therefore all unbuilt; the closest formalised material is upstream of F0 rather than inside it.

targets.target: A_inf = W(𝒪_F) for a characteristic-p perfectoid field F, with its (p,[ϖ])-adic topology, complete Hausdorff Huber-ring structure and Witt Frobenius/Teichmüller
targets.note: Mathlib has W(R) for any commutative ring with Frobenius, Teichmüller and (for perfect R) `frobeniusEquiv`, supplies a characteristic-p perfect valued field as `Tilt K v O hv p` (the tilt of a valued field, with the valuation `PreTilt.val` on its ring `PreTilt O p`, though completeness of the tilt is not proved), and Tau Ceti has the general Huber-ring/pair-of-definition API; but no file puts a topology on W(𝒪_F), and grep finds no `A_inf`/`Ainf` anywhere in either tree. Completeness and separatedness of the (p,[ϖ])-adic topology, and the statement that A_inf is Huber but not Tate, are unproved.

targets.target: The open locus 𝒴_F = D(p) ∩ D([ϖ]) inside Spa(A_inf, A_inf), its openness, nonemptiness and Frobenius stability
targets.note: Tau Ceti builds Spa(A,A⁺) as a set of continuous valuations, rational subsets, and the analytic locus with its finite rational cover — the machinery the layer needs — but the particular locus `v(p[ϖ]) ≠ 0` for A_inf does not exist, and the layer's own warning that it differs from the analytic locus D(p) ∪ D([ϖ]) has no counterpart in the library.

targets.target: The Frobenius quotient X_F = 𝒴_F/φ^ℤ together with q : 𝒴_F → X_F, wandering charts and local chart isomorphisms
targets.note: No declaration in either tree mentions a Frobenius quotient of an adic spectrum, wandering windows or a quotient adic space; `grep -rn -i wandering` over both trees returns nothing.

targets.target: Interface statements for D6: analytic adic structure over ℤ_p and factorisation of the structure morphism over Spa(ℚ_p,ℤ_p) as a morphism in a category of adic spaces
targets.note: ℚ_p is proved to be a Tate Huber ring with pair of definition (ℤ_p,(p)) and ℤ_p a non-Tate Huber ring, so the base pair exists at ring level. There is no category of adic spaces and no notion of a morphism Spa(A,A⁺) → Spa(B,B⁺) as a locally-ringed-space map; only `comap` on the underlying valuation spectra (Spa/Comap.lean) is available.

targets.target: Transport through the independence-of-ϖ isomorphisms
targets.note: There is a general `IsPseudoUniformizer` predicate in Tau Ceti (TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/Basic.lean), but no statement comparing constructions made with two different pseudouniformisers.

duplicates.note: §6.1–6.2 of AdicSpaces Layer 6 construct exactly the same objects — A_inf = W(𝒪_F) with pair of definition (A_inf,(p,[ϖ])), 𝒴 = D(p)∩D([ϖ]), the Frobenius windows U_n/V_n and the quotient 𝒳 = 𝒴/φ^ℤ — and F0 explicitly says it consumes them; F0 adds only the interface lemmas needed by D6.
Builds the same integral period space in the relative setting, `𝒴_S = Spa(W_{O_E}(R⁺)) \ V([ϖ])` with the (π,[ϖ])-adic topology, specialising to F0's fixed-field case when S = Spa(F,𝒪_F) and E = ℚ_p.

targets.target: The functor of points of 𝒴_F^♢ on characteristic-p perfectoid test objects, i.e. diamondification of an analytic adic space
targets.note: Neither library defines Perf, v-sheaves, diamonds or the functor X ↦ X^♢; a case-insensitive grep for `diamond` in the Lean trees returns only `Mathlib/GroupTheory/FreeGroup/Basic.lean` (the diamond lemma) and Tau Ceti's modular-forms diamond operators.

targets.target: Spd(ℚ_p) as the v-sheaf of untilts over ℚ_p, and the representable sheaf S = Spa(F,𝒪_F) on Perf
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'Spd'` over both trees finds no such object. There is no site of perfectoid spaces to represent a sheaf on.

targets.target: Identification of continuous maps W(𝒪_F) → 𝒪⁺(T^♯) with maps into the integral tilt, via the universal property of Witt vectors of a perfect ring and Fontaine's θ
targets.note: Mathlib has the algebraic ingredients: the integral tilt `PreTilt O p` with its ℝ≥0-valuation `PreTilt.val` and the multiplicative sharp map `PreTilt.untilt`, the universal property `WittVector.lift` for p-adically complete targets, and `fontaineTheta : 𝕎 R♭ →+* R` with surjectivity under Frobenius-surjectivity of R/p. What is missing is the continuity/boundedness half of the statement — the identification is proved only as a map of untopologised rings, exactly what the layer says is not enough — and there is no notion of an untilt of a perfectoid *space* with its 𝒪⁺.

targets.target: The isomorphism α_F : 𝒴_F^♢ ≃ S × Spd(ℚ_p) of v-sheaves/locally spatial diamonds, with both directions, inverse-ness, and gluing over affinoid covers
targets.note: Nothing of this statement can be formed: none of 𝒴_F, (−)^♢, Spd ℚ_p or the v-topology exists.

duplicates.note: States the same untilt product formula (FS II.1.2, `𝒴_S^♢ ≅ S × Spd(O_E)`) in the relative form; F1 is its E = ℚ_p, S = Spa(F,𝒪_F) specialisation.
Constructs Spd ℤ_p and Spd(A,A⁺) by marked untilts with v-descent, which is the right-hand factor of F1's bijection.
Owns the classification of marked untilts by primitive degree-one ideals and Fontaine's θ with its kernel, the algebraic engine of F1's bijection.

targets.target: Frobenius φ_Y on 𝒴_F induced by Witt Frobenius, absolute Frobenius φ_S on S, and the equivariance α_F ∘ φ_Y^♢ = (φ_S × id) ∘ α_F
targets.note: Witt Frobenius and the absolute p-power Frobenius of a characteristic-p ring both exist in Mathlib, including their compatibility with Teichmüller lifts; the induced action on an adic spectrum (by precomposition on valuations) and the equivariance statement do not exist because 𝒴_F does not.

targets.target: The ℤ-action is free with wandering charts, q is locally an isomorphism, and its relation is the disjoint union of Frobenius graphs ∐_{n∈ℤ} 𝒴_F^♢ ≃ 𝒴_F^♢ ×_{X_F^♢} 𝒴_F^♢
targets.note: No quotient of an adic spectrum by a Frobenius action is constructed anywhere in either tree, so freeness, wandering windows and the groupoid relation have no counterpart.

targets.target: Effectivity of the étale relation after diamondification and the identification β_F : X_F^♢ ≃ (S × Spd ℚ_p)/(φ_S^ℤ × id), over Spd ℚ_p and independent of ϖ
targets.note: Requires the whole diamond formalism, which is absent.

duplicates.note: Establishes the q-Frobenius action, wandering annuli and the adic quotient X_S = Y_S/φ^ℤ with descent in the relative setting, and explicitly says its ℚ_p fixed-field specialisation is to be compared with FarguesFontaineDiamonds F1–F3.
§6.2 already owns the Frobenius radius law κ(φ(v)) = p·κ(v), freeness of the ℤ-action, the wandering windows and the quotient space 𝒳; F2 reuses those and adds only the diamond-level statements.

targets.target: Equivalence of étale sites (X_F)_ét ≃ (X_F^♢)_ét
targets.note: Neither an étale site of an adic space nor the étale site of a diamond exists. Mathlib has étale sites only for schemes (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean) and the pro-étale site of schemes (Sites/Proetale.lean); neither is the adic-space notion.

targets.target: Equivalence of finite étale categories (X_F)_fét ≃ (X_F^♢)_fét, compatibility with covers, restriction to the wandering charts through α_F and β_F
targets.note: No finite étale category of adic spaces is defined in Tau Ceti; the AdicSpace tree stops at the structure presheaf and sheaf criteria.

targets.target: Étale sheaf descent along q^♢ including the Frobenius cocycle, as an equivalence of categories with descent data
targets.note: General sheaf-descent machinery exists in Mathlib's `CategoryTheory/Sites/Descent` and `DenseSubsite`, but there is no adic or diamond site on which to instantiate it, and no Frobenius-cocycle statement.

duplicates.note: Owns the general adic-to-diamond étale and finite-étale site comparison (ECD Lemma 15.6); F3 is the instance of that general theorem at X_F, as D6's own test list says.
Includes the diamond formulas for the relative curve and their comparison with FarguesFontaineDiamonds F1–F3.

Owns the analytic finite-stage inputs to the same comparison — uniform completion of a Tate pair, invariance of its valuation spectrum and the étale-category comparison of ECD 15.3–15.4 — which is the local form of F3's site equivalence.

targets.target: Sections of 𝒴_F^♢ → S as marked untilts of S over ℚ_p, and the map from an untilt to 𝒴_F
targets.note: Mathlib has the ring-level untilt (`PreTilt.untilt`, the sharp map) of a p-adically complete ring, but not marked untilts of a perfectoid space, nor the classification of untilts by primitive degree-one ideals; and 𝒴_F is absent.

targets.target: The primitive kernel of θ as a local equation, and the proof that it cuts out a closed Cartier divisor (not merely principality in the Witt ring)
targets.note: `fontaineTheta` and its surjectivity are proved, and `BDeRhamPlus` is defined as the adic completion along ker(θ[1/p]); but Mathlib never proves that ker θ is principal generated by a non-zero-divisor (the `BDeRham` docstring says this is only 'mathematically equivalent' and inverts all generators to dodge it), and there is no divisor-theoretic statement. Tau Ceti's Cartier divisors (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/CartierDivisor) are for schemes, not adic spaces.

targets.target: Injectivity and closed image of multiplication by the primitive generator on annular neighbourhoods; identification of the completed quotient with the untilt algebra; the exact sequence of analytic sheaves
targets.note: No analytic sheaves on an adic annulus over A_inf exist; Tau Ceti's structure presheaf is built only for a general Huber pair and no such exactness statement is present.

targets.target: Perfectoidness of compatible-root base extensions of period annuli, the tilt computation, and the maximum-modulus / Shilov-boundary lower bound for multiplication by the primitive generator
targets.note: `Perfectoid` as a property of a Tate ring is not defined anywhere in either tree (Mathlib's `RingTheory/Perfectoid/` contains only θ, B_dR and untilt); there is no Shilov boundary or maximum-modulus principle for adic annuli.

targets.target: Descent of the divisor to X_F along Frobenius translates, and dependence only on the Frobenius orbit; Div¹ = Spd ℚ_p/φ^ℤ kept distinct from X_F^♢
targets.note: Requires the quotient and the diamond formalism, both absent.

duplicates.note: States the identical content — marked untilts over E, the primitive kernel of θ, its Cartier divisor on Y_S and X_S, injectivity and closed image of multiplication by a local generator, and Div¹ — in the relative setting.
Owns Div^d and the degree-d Cartier divisors on 𝒴_S, of which F4's single marked untilt is the degree-one fixed-field case.
F4 cites it for the integral perfectoid criteria used in the base-extension argument, so the perfectoidness half of F4's analytic input is owned there.

targets.target: Lift of the étale-site comparison to left-completed derived categories for the allowed coefficients, with compatibility with pullback and tensor
targets.note: There is no left-completed derived category of a site in Mathlib (no `leftCompletion` of a derived category), and no étale derived category of an adic space or diamond.

targets.target: RΓ((X_F)_ét, A) ≃ RΓ((X_F^♢)_ét, A^♢) in the specified range
targets.note: Mathlib has global sections of sheaves on an arbitrary site and derived functors in the abstract, but neither of the two sites in the statement exists, so the comparison cannot be stated.

targets.target: Adic coefficients with derived completion and the finite-level comparisons
targets.note: Derived I-adic completion of a derived category of sheaves does not exist in either tree; Mathlib's `AdicCompletion` is a module-level construction.

targets.target: Geometric hypotheses (properness, smoothness, dualizing complex) for Rf_! / Rf^! on X_F^♢ → Spd ℚ_p
targets.note: The six operations do not exist for any adic or diamond geometry in either library.

duplicates.note: Owns the construction of the left-completed étale derived category D_ét and its hyperdescent; F5 only instantiates it on X_F and is explicitly gated on C2.
Owns the adic-coefficient category with derived I-completeness and the finite-level comparisons that F5's second paragraph defers to.

FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeThe.summary: One of this roadmap's headline targets is already fully formalised: Tau Ceti proves Cartier duality for finite locally free commutative affine group schemes over an *arbitrary* commutative base ring, as an anti-equivalence of categories, with involutivity, naturality and base change, and with no sorry in any of the four files. Around it sit useful but partial inputs — Tau Ceti's finite-dual Hopf-algebra package, its identity component / finite-étale component group over an algebraically closed field, its fppf quotient sheaves and faithfully-flat descent; Mathlib's fppf/fpqc topologies with subcanonicality and descent of morphism properties, Witt vectors with Frobenius, Verschiebung and FV = p, F-isocrystals with the one-dimensional Dieudonné–Manin classification, divided powers, Eisenstein polynomials and the cyclotomic character. Everything specifically integral-p-adic is missing: there is no p-divisible group, no Tate module of anything, no Dieudonné module, no Fontaine–Laffaille or Breuil–Kisin module, no Serre weight, no deformation functor anywhere in either library (`grep -rli deformation` returns four unrelated files), and no higher ramification filtration in upper numbering. R07.1 is partly built; R07.2–R07.6 are not built.

targets.target: Cartier duality for finite locally free commutative group schemes over the allowed bases, with involutivity and base change
targets.note: Fully present and more general than asked: `cartierDuality R` is an anti-equivalence of the category of finite locally free commutative affine group schemes over Spec R with itself for an arbitrary `CommRing R` (not merely a mixed-characteristic DVR), `cartierDualDualNatIso` is the double-dual natural isomorphism, and `baseChangeDualNatIso` gives compatibility with base change. `grep -c sorry` is 0 in all four Cartier-duality files. The roadmap's own 'Existing material' paragraph lists this as work to be done here or in ModularCurves #81.

targets.target: Connected–étale sequence of a finite locally free group scheme over a henselian local / complete local base, functorial and compatible with base change
targets.note: Tau Ceti constructs the identity-component Hopf ideal, the fppf quotient π₀(G) and proves it is a finite étale constant group scheme — but only for finite-type affine group schemes over an *algebraically closed field*, and only as the quotient, not as a short exact sequence over a henselian local ring. The mixed-characteristic statement the layer needs, and the splitting over a perfect residue field, are absent.

targets.target: Generic and special fibres, finite-flat subgroup and quotient constructions
targets.note: Tau Ceti has fppf quotients of affine group schemes by normal Hopf ideals and faithfully-flat descent for Hopf-algebra maps; Mathlib has base change and fibres of schemes in general. What is absent is the finite-flat quotient of a finite locally free group scheme by a finite locally free subgroup over a DVR, and the generic/special-fibre dictionary for it.

targets.target: fpqc descent for finite flat commutative group schemes
targets.note: Mathlib defines the fppf and fpqc topologies on schemes, proves both subcanonical (anonymous instances in `Sites/Fpqc.lean`), proves many morphism properties descend along surjective flat quasi-compact maps, and has a general `DescentData`/`IsStack` framework; but no file proves that quasi-coherent sheaves (hence finite flat group schemes) form an fpqc stack, so the descent statement the layer needs is not available.

targets.target: p-divisible group as a compatible system of finite locally free levels with exactness and rank conditions
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'p-divisible\|pDivisible\|Barsotti'` over both Lean trees returns nothing. Only Mathlib's `AddGroup.IsDivisible` (a completely different notion) matches on the word.

targets.target: Tate module of a p-divisible group, and comparison of duality with the cyclotomic twist
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'tate module'` finds nothing in either tree — there is no Tate module of an elliptic curve, abelian variety or p-divisible group anywhere. Only the twisting character exists: Mathlib's p-adic `cyclotomicCharacter` of a field automorphism, with its mod-p^n reductions.

targets.target: Finite-flat closure of a generic subgroup scheme under the correct base hypotheses (scheme-theoretic closure)
targets.note: Mathlib has scheme-theoretic image (`AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Basic`/`IdealSheaf`) but no flatness statement for the closure of a subgroup of the generic fibre over a DVR.

targets.target: Raynaud's generic-fibre full faithfulness/uniqueness (Cor. 3.3.6) for p-primary finite flat commutative group schemes over a mixed-characteristic DVR with e < p−1, with flatness of the extended kernel/cokernel and Ext-injectivity
targets.note: `grep -rn -i raynaud` over both trees returns nothing; no theorem in either library mentions the absolute ramification bound e < p−1.

targets.target: The (p,…,p)-type classification of Raynaud group schemes and its tame inertia characters
targets.note: Nothing in either tree defines a group scheme of type (p,…,p), a fundamental character of level n, or tame inertia. The only inertia notion available is `ValuationSubring.inertiaSubgroup`, the kernel of the decomposition group acting on the residue field, with no ramification filtration above it.

duplicates.note: Owns finite locally free group schemes and Cartier duality (SGA 3 VII_A §3.3, KM §1.12) for the elliptic-curve setting; R07.1's Cartier-duality target is the same theorem, and the Tau Ceti library declaration cited above discharges both.

Its PD-1 constructs the p-divisible group E[p^∞] as compatible finite locally free levels with the rank and epimorphism conditions, and PD-2 constructs the connected–étale sequence over a henselian local ring — exactly R07.1's second and fifth targets, in the elliptic-curve case.
States the finite-flat quotient, the fppf quotient abelian scheme, Weil pairings and Tate-module pairings; it explicitly imports Cartier duality from R07.1, so the two layers share that target.
Restates p-divisible groups with their Cartier duals, Tate modules and duality over 𝒪_K, so T0 and R07.1 overlap on the p-divisible-group and duality targets.

targets.target: Dieudonné modules over a perfect residue field and the (anti)equivalence with finite commutative p-group schemes / p-divisible groups
targets.note: `grep -i dieudonn` over both trees hits only Tau Ceti's Cartan–Dieudonné theorem for orthogonal groups (`TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/CartanDieudonne.lean` and `TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/CartanDieudonne/`), a wholly unrelated result. No Dieudonné ring, module or functor exists.

targets.target: Frobenius and Verschiebung with the relation FV = VF = p
targets.note: Mathlib proves F∘V = V∘F = multiplication by p on Witt vectors of a characteristic-p ring, which is the scalar side of the Dieudonné ring; but the Dieudonné ring W(k)[F,V] itself and its module category are never formed, so 'Frobenius and Verschiebung of a Dieudonné module' does not exist.

targets.target: Dimensions, heights and slopes, with the ordinary and supersingular cases
targets.note: Mathlib has F-isocrystals over a perfect field (a K(p,k)-space with a σ-semilinear automorphism), the standard slope-m one-dimensional objects, and the Dieudonné–Manin classification *only in dimension one over an algebraically closed field*. Heights and dimensions of p-divisible groups, and the words ordinary/supersingular, appear nowhere (`grep -i supersingular` over both trees is empty).

targets.target: Deformation of p-divisible groups over nilpotent thickenings (Grothendieck–Messing-type results)
targets.note: There is no deformation theory in either library. Mathlib's `RingTheory/DividedPowers` supplies PD-structures on ideals, which is the right base ingredient for a PD-thickening, but no crystal, no Messing crystal and no deformation functor is built on top of it.

duplicates.note: Owns isocrystals, the slope conventions and the full Dieudonné–Manin classification over an algebraically closed residue base, which is R07.2's slope target stated in the geometric-Langlands setting.
Imports p-divisible groups and Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory from R07.2/R07.6 and proves Serre–Tate; the deformation target is shared.
Owns crystalline sites, structure sheaves and crystals, the framework in which R07.2's deformation results over nilpotent thickenings are normally proved; R07.2 lists CR.0/CR.1 as its prerequisites.

targets.target: The category of integral filtered Frobenius modules (Fontaine–Laffaille modules) over an absolutely unramified base
targets.note: `grep -i 'laffaille'` over both trees is empty. Mathlib has a general `IsFiltration`/`IsModuleFiltration` API for filtrations indexed by an ordered monoid, and Witt-vector Frobenius, but nothing combining a decreasing filtration with divided Frobenii φ_i and the strong-divisibility condition.

targets.target: The Galois functor from Fontaine–Laffaille modules to ℤ_p-representations, its exactness and full faithfulness on [0,p−2]
targets.note: No p-adic Galois representation category exists in either library, let alone this functor. Mathlib's `Mathlib/RepresentationTheory` is abstract representation theory with no continuity or p-adic structure.

targets.target: Identification of the finite-flat and crystalline examples, and the effect of torsion subquotients and reductions on the filtration
targets.note: `grep -i crystalline` over both trees returns no declarations; there is no crystalline representation, no admissible filtered φ-module, and no finite-flat model.

targets.target: Endpoint full faithfulness on the restricted subcategories at [0,p−1], and the safe interval [0,0] at p = 2
targets.note: Requires the previous two targets; nothing in either library refers to Fontaine–Laffaille weight ranges.

duplicates.note: 'Fontaine–Laffaille weights and degree shifting' restates the same weight-range bookkeeping for the automorphy-lifting application.

The 'Integral and small-weight interface' layer in this same batch also names Fontaine–Laffaille and Breuil–Kisin integral theory as its content; R07.3 and R06.4 overlap on the small-weight integral comparison.
Uses Fontaine–Laffaille torsion comparison for integral torsion inequalities and lattice recovery, restating the torsion-subquotient behaviour R07.3 owns.

targets.target: The Breuil–Kisin coefficient ring 𝞢 = W(k)[[u]] with its Frobenius, and the Eisenstein polynomial of a uniformiser
targets.note: Both ingredients exist separately — Mathlib's `PowerSeries` over any commutative ring (so W(k)[[u]] is expressible) and `Polynomial.IsEisensteinAt` — but there is no declaration equipping W(k)[[u]] with the Frobenius u ↦ u^p extending Witt Frobenius, and `grep -i 'breuil\|kisin'` over both trees is empty.

targets.target: Frobenius modules of bounded height over 𝞢, with the height bound determined by E(u)
targets.note: No φ-module over a power-series ring with an E(u)-height condition is defined anywhere.

targets.target: Classification of finite flat group schemes and p-divisible groups by Breuil–Kisin modules, with descent data and generic-fibre comparison
targets.note: Requires p-divisible groups (absent) and the module category above (absent).

targets.target: Separation of the finite-flat, potentially Barsotti–Tate and potentially semistable cases, including the dyadic theorem
targets.note: None of these representation-theoretic conditions is defined in either library.

duplicates.note: Also in this batch; its integral interface names Breuil–Kisin modules and the same coefficient ring, so the coefficient-ring and φ-module targets are shared.
'Prismatic F-crystals and crystalline lattices' builds the Breuil–Kisin prism and the equivalence with lattices in crystalline representations, the modern form of R07.4's classification.
'Cohomological Breuil–Kisin descent and cross-theory interfaces' reuses the same Breuil–Kisin module category from the cohomological side.
Its dyadic and endpoint cases consume the p = 2 Breuil–Kisin branch R07.4 promises to prove.

targets.target: Inertia characters of the p-torsion of a good ordinary or supersingular elliptic curve
targets.note: Neither `supersingular` nor `ordinary` occurs as a declaration in either tree, and there is no Galois action on elliptic-curve torsion: Tau Ceti has division polynomials and torsion points (`TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/DivisionPolynomial/Torsion`), but no Galois representation attached to them. `ValuationSubring.inertiaSubgroup` is the only inertia group available and carries no ramification filtration.

targets.target: Extension-sensitive finite-flat criteria and the peu-ramifiée / très-ramifiée distinction, with the extension-class computations
targets.note: `grep -i 'ramifiée\|peu.ramif\|tres.ramif'` over both trees returns nothing; there is no Ext computation for finite flat group schemes.

targets.target: Finite-flat generic-fibre calculations feeding the p = 2 Serre-weight dichotomy and the weight-two criterion for p ≥ 5
targets.note: No Serre weight is defined anywhere (`grep -i serreweight` is empty) and there is no finite-flat model theory to compute with.

duplicates.note: 'Weight optimisation at p' owns the Serre-weight recipe that R07.5's computations feed; the two layers state the same local residual dichotomy from opposite ends.
Its exact source decomposition covers the same peu/très ramifiée weight prescription.
R07.1 explicitly promises the (p,…,p)-type classification and its tame inertia characters 'used in R07.5', so the tame-inertia-character target is stated twice inside this roadmap.

targets.target: Deformation-theoretic tangent and obstruction calculations for integral local deformation conditions
targets.note: There is no deformation functor, no Schlessinger/Rim criterion and no tangent-obstruction formalism in either library: `grep -rli deformation` over both Lean trees returns only `Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FontaineTheta.lean` (the word in a docstring), a Burau-representation file, a chain-homotopy file and a homotopy-group file.

targets.target: Ramification bounds on torsion of finite-flat / p-divisible groups: Fontaine's cutoff u > e(n + 1/(p−1)) in the shifted upper-numbering convention, with the normalised different bound
targets.note: Mathlib has `differentIdeal` for a finite extension of Dedekind domains, and Tau Ceti has the *lower*-numbering ramification filtration G_i, but only for places of function fields. Neither library has the Herbrand function, upper numbering G^(u), or any bound on ramification coming from a finite flat group scheme, so the statement cannot even be formed.

targets.target: Comparison of finite-flat models under field extension and twisting, and stability of a local deformation condition under those operations
targets.note: Requires finite-flat models (absent) and deformation conditions (absent).

targets.target: Galois-module comparison for abelian-scheme torsion
targets.note: There is no Galois action on torsion of an abelian scheme in either library; Tau Ceti's abelian-variety files (`TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AbelianVariety/`) cover endomorphisms and homomorphisms, not Galois modules.

duplicates.note: Names R07.6 as the source of Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory and proves Serre–Tate from it, so the deformation target is shared.
'Newton strata, central leaves and local deformation data' restates the local deformation theory of p-divisible groups in the Shimura-variety setting.
'Restriction, twisting and change of problem' owns the stability of a deformation condition under field extension and twisting that R07.6 also states.

HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups.summary: This roadmap sits almost entirely outside both libraries. There is no p-divisible group, no Tate module, no Hodge–Tate map, no perfectoid space, no pro-étale site of an adic space, no period sheaf, no Shimura or modular variety as a scheme, no canonical subgroup, no Hasse invariant, no Igusa tower and no logarithmic geometry of any kind (`grep -i 'logStructure\|LogScheme\|Kummer.*etale'` over both Lean trees is empty). The only genuinely usable inputs are Tau Ceti's Cartier duality for finite locally free commutative group schemes over any base, its conormal/cotangent space of a Hopf ideal, its abelian varieties over a field, and Mathlib's Fontaine θ with `BDeRhamPlus`/`BDeRham` as bare definitions plus `Module.Grassmannian` for the flag-variety target. What is missing is everything T0–T6 states: the Hodge–Tate map at finite and infinite level, the Hodge–Tate exact sequence and its Levi torsor, canonical subgroups with their quantitative ε-bounds, the anticanonical tower and period estimates, the Igusa torsors and the modified lattice ω^int, and the whole Kummer-étale/pro-Kummer-étale log formalism with its logarithmic Poincaré lemma. All nine layers are not built.

There is no p-divisible group in either library, so its dual, height and Lie algebra are unavailable.

targets.target: Generic-fibre Tate modules of the p-divisible group

targets.note: Mathlib has Kähler differentials of a ring extension and Tau Ceti the cotangent space of an affine group scheme, but nothing computes ω_G for a p-divisible group or defines a Hodge ideal; `grep -i hodgeideal` over both trees is empty.

targets.target: Extension to semi-abelian degeneration charts with explicit toric and abelian pieces
targets.note: Tau Ceti has abelian varieties over a field (isogenies, endomorphism ring, tangent space) but no abelian schemes over a general base, no semi-abelian schemes and no degeneration data; `grep -i 'semiabelian\|semi.abelian\|degeneration'` over both trees returns nothing.

targets.target: The finite-level Hodge–Tate map built from Cartier duality and differentials of characters, with functoriality, compatibility with endomorphisms and polarisations, and passage to the completed p-adic map
targets.note: No Hodge–Tate map exists in either library. The only declarations matching 'Hodge' and 'Tate' together are Tau Ceti's complex Hodge structures and their Tate twist ℚ(n) (`TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/Tate/`), an unrelated object over ℂ.

PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomo.summary: Nothing in this roadmap has been formalised. Both Lean trees are empty of `Robba`, `dagger`, `overconvergent`, `Newton polygon`, `crystalline`, `rigid cohomology`, `frame`, `strict neighbourhood`, `trace formula` and any zeta function of a variety over a finite field. The usable inputs are Tau Ceti's Huber/Wedhorn analytic package — restricted and weighted restricted power series, the two-sided series ring A⟨X,X⁻¹⟩ of Wedhorn Example 6.39, Laurent localisations and their complete separated topologies — which is genuinely the right starting material for RD.0's annulus rings but is built for a fixed radius over an arbitrary Tate ring rather than as a radius-indexed family with norms λ_r; Mathlib's Witt Frobenius and F-isocrystals with the one-dimensional Dieudonné–Manin classification; Mathlib's `Derivation`/`Differential` and Kähler differentials; and a bare definition of ℓ-adic cohomology of a scheme via the pro-étale site. Every mathematical target of RD.0–RD.7 — Robba rings, generic radii and slope filtrations, the p-adic local monodromy theorem, overconvergent isocrystals on frames, rigid cohomology with compact support, finiteness/duality/Künneth, the rigid Lefschetz trace formula with p-adic weights, and the rigid–crystalline comparison — is missing. All eight layers are not built.

targets.target: Overconvergent (dagger) power-series algebras as unions over strict radii, with weak completion maps
targets.note: `grep -i 'dagger\|overconvergent\|weaklyComplete'` over both Lean trees returns nothing. Tau Ceti does have Wedhorn's restricted power series A⟨X⟩ and weighted restricted power series A⟨X⟩_T with their topologies and completions, and the closed polydisc Spa(A⟨T⟩, A⟨T⟩°) with its classical points — the fixed-radius affinoid side; the union over shrinking radii, weak completion, and the separation of an overconvergent algebra from its affinoid completion that the acceptance test demands are all absent.

targets.target: Bounded and full Robba rings with radius-indexed norms and topology
targets.note: The closest object in either library is Tau Ceti's `twoSidedRestrictedSubmodule`, the coefficient module of A⟨X,X⁻¹⟩ (Wedhorn Example 6.39) for a Tate ring A, i.e. functions on one closed annulus of radius 1; Laurent rational localisations and their complete separated presentations also exist. There is no family of norms λ_r, no restriction map between annuli of different radii, and no colimit over r → 1⁻, so neither the bounded nor the full Robba ring exists.

targets.target: Differential forms on these algebras and the exterior derivative
targets.note: Mathlib's `Derivation` and `KaehlerDifferential` give Ω¹ of a ring extension algebraically, but there is no continuous/analytic version for a dagger or Robba ring and no de Rham complex in either library.

targets.target: Flatness, faithful descent and base-change lemmas for these coefficient rings
targets.note: Mathlib has the general flat/faithfully-flat module theory and Tau Ceti proves base change for restricted power series and flatness of Laurent localisations (`Huber/LocalizationTopology/Laurent/Flat.lean`); none of it is stated for the rings this layer builds, which do not exist.

targets.target: Compatible Frobenius lifts on the coefficient rings and the dependence on the coordinate
targets.note: Witt-vector Frobenius exists; a Frobenius lift φ on a dagger or Robba ring with φ(x) ≡ x^p, and the comparison of two coordinate choices, do not.

duplicates.note: Also in this batch; it constructs 'the bounded, overconvergent and Robba coefficient rings from actual convergent Laurent series on annuli, their norms/topologies and restriction maps' — the same objects as RD.0, and RD.0 names it as an input.

Owns weakly complete dagger affinoid algebras, radius-indexed presentations, strict neighbourhoods, dagger differential forms and the exterior derivative; RD.0 lists it as an input yet restates the same constructions.
Constructs the cyclotomic coefficient rings A_K, B_K and their overconvergent variants with commuting φ and Γ actions, overlapping RD.0's Robba rings and Frobenius lifts.

targets.target: Finite projective differential modules over a Robba ring, with horizontal Frobenius structures
targets.note: Mathlib has `Differential` (a commutative ring with a chosen derivation) and `DifferentialAlgebra`, developed for Liouville-type differential field theory, plus projective modules; but no module-with-connection over a differential ring and no Frobenius structure on one. The base Robba ring is itself absent.

targets.target: Generic radii of convergence and cyclic-vector reduction
targets.note: No radius of convergence of a differential module and no cyclic-vector theorem appear in either library; `grep -i 'cyclic vector'` returns nothing.

targets.target: Frobenius pullback and the slope filtration, with existence, uniqueness, descent and coefficient extensions
targets.note: The only slope theory in either library is Mathlib's F-isocrystals over a perfect field: the standard slope-m one-dimensional objects and the classification of one-dimensional isocrystals over an algebraically closed field. targets.note: Neither invariant is defined in either library.

targets.note: `grep -i 'local monodromy\|quasi-unipotent'` over both Lean trees returns nothing. All three ingredients — the Robba ring, differential modules and Frobenius structures — are missing, so the statement cannot be formed.

targets.target: The resulting filtration and logarithmic solutions, with descent and compatibility
targets.note: No logarithmic solution or nilpotent-residue statement exists in either library.

targets.note: No rigid cohomology to compare; Mathlib's triangulated-category machinery is present but has nothing to be applied to here.

PadicHodgeTheory.summary: Mathlib has substantially more of this roadmap's starting point than the document records. ℂ_[p] is constructed as the completion of an algebraic closure of ℚ_p and proved algebraically closed and nonarchimedean, with its valuation subring 𝓞_ℂ_[p]; Scholze’s tilt of a valued field (`Tilt`, with the valuation `PreTilt.val`) is built in the generality that applies to it; Fontaine's θ : 𝕎(R♭) → R is constructed and proved surjective when Frobenius is surjective on R/p, the tilt R♭ = `PreTilt` and the sharp map `PreTilt.untilt` exist for any p-adically complete ring, and `BDeRhamPlus`/`BDeRham` are defined as the ker(θ[1/p])-adic completion of 𝕎(R♭)[1/p] and its localisation — more general than the O_C case R06.1 asks for, and sorry-free. That is where the coverage stops: nothing is proved about these rings (the whole `BDeRham.lean` file is three definitions), ker θ is never shown to be principal, there is no filtration, no Galois action, and B_cris^+, B_cris and B_st do not exist at all. None of D_HT/D_dR/D_cris/D_st, admissibility, filtered (φ,N)-modules, (φ,Γ)-modules, Robba rings, period sheaves, the p-adic monodromy theorem or any geometric comparison theorem is present; ℓ-adic cohomology of a scheme exists only as a bare definition. R06.1 is partly built on the strength of ℂ_[p], the tilt, θ and the two B_dR definitions; the other nine layers are not built.

targets.note: Both halves are in Mathlib and sorry-free. `PadicComplex p = ℂ_[p]` is the completion of `AlgebraicClosure ℚ_p` for the spectral norm, proved algebraically closed, of characteristic zero and nonarchimedean, with a rank-one ℝ≥0-valuation and `valuation_p : v p = 1/p`; `PadicComplexInt p = 𝓞_ℂ_[p]` is its valuation subring, with `PadicComplexInt.integers`. `Tilt K v O hv p`, Scholze’s tilt of a valued field, is the fraction field of `PreTilt O p`, and `PreTilt.val` is its ℝ≥0-valuation; its three hypotheses (`Fact p.Prime`, `Valuation.Integers v O`, `Fact (v p ≠ 1)`) are exactly what the ℂ_[p] file supplies, so C_p♭ is this construction instantiated. Mathlib does not write that instantiation down, and does not prove 𝓞_ℂ_[p] is p-adically complete (no `IsAdicComplete` instance), which the θ and B_dR files take as a hypothesis.

review.notes: Re-checked all 202 declaration citations: 197 match declarations.tsv on name, library, file and line. Of the five that do not, four are the audit's and are right: TauCeti.FiniteLocallyFreeCommAffineGroupSchemeCat.cartierDuality and cartierDualDualNatIso do carry the TauCeti prefix — CartierDuality/FiniteLocallyFree.lean opens `namespace TauCeti` at line 65 and closes it at 350, with `namespace FiniteLocallyFreeCommAffineGroupSchemeCat` at 220 inside it — and declarations.tsv drops it because index_declarations.py matches `namespace` only when the name is on the same line, while that file writes the name on the next line and closes the block with a bare `end`, popping TauCeti off the indexer's stack. The fifth was a wrong line number and is corrected. No cited file (73 of them) contains a sorry. Layer coverage is exact (39 of 39, none extra) and all 115 duplicates resolve to atlas stages. The four targets claimed present were read in the source and hold: Tau Ceti's Cartier duality is an anti-equivalence over an arbitrary CommRing with double-dual and base-change natural isomorphisms, and Mathlib's PadicComplex/Tilt, fontaineTheta with its surjectivity and Teichmüller formula, and BDeRhamPlus/BDeRham are as described — including the note's caveat that the docstring's claim of agreement with the classical de Rham period ring is not itself proved. Independently re-searched the absent and partial claims by concept over both trees: no p-divisible or Barsotti-Tate groups, no Dieudonné module or ring, no Fontaine-Laffaille or Breuil-Kisin modules, no canonical subgroups, Hasse invariants or Igusa towers, no Tate curve, no B_cris/B_st or weak admissibility, no rigid cohomology, dagger algebras, log adic spaces or Newton polygons. The audit's own false-friend checks hold: the only Dieudonné in either tree is Cartan-Dieudonné, the 130 monodromy declarations are covering-space monodromy, and the 264 slope declarations are convexity, derivatives and Dehn-surgery slopes. R07.4's duplicate list already names PrismaticCohomology:PR.7, which is the mirror of a duplicate added to PR.7 in REV-AUDIT-38 on the same day, so the two audits agree in both directions.
